content: Econazole is a topical antifungal medication used to treat various skin infections, including athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm. It may also be prescribed for other conditions as determined by your doctor. Always consult your healthcare provider or pharmacist for additional information regarding its use. Econazole is available as a cream that is applied directly to the skin. Typically, it is used once or twice daily, in the morning and evening, for a duration of two weeks. However, certain infections may require treatment for up to six weeks. Follow the instructions provided on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions or concerns, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Use the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Before application, clean the affected area thoroughly, allow it to dry, and then gently rub the cream into the skin until most of it is absorbed. Use only enough to cover the infected area. Wash your hands after applying the medication unless the treatment is for your hands. Continue using econazole for the full duration of the prescribed treatment, even if your symptoms improve. Do not discontinue use without consulting your doctor. Before starting econazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to econazole or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs, including vitamins and supplements, that you are currently taking. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. Should you become pregnant while using econazole, contact your healthcare provider immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed application. Econazole may cause side effects. If you experience symptoms such as itching, burning, irritation, stinging, redness, or rash, contact your doctor immediately. For severe side effects, you or your doctor can report them to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store econazole in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. Econazole is intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, mouth, or ingestion of the medication. Do not apply cosmetics, lotions, or other skin products to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If your symptoms persist after completing the prescribed course, contact your doctor. Keep all follow-up appointments with your healthcare provider. If you have any questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. The brand name for econazole is Spectazole®.
